memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The son of Dan: Hushim. The sons of Naphtali: Jahziel, Guni, Jezer and Shillem. These were the sons born to Jacob by Bilhah, whom Laban had given to his daughter Rachel—seven in all." — Gen 46:23-25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The smallest branch of the family. Bilhah's line accounts for seven people out of seventy. Dan has just one son listed.

Small numbers do not trouble God. Dan and Naphtali became full tribes with a full inheritance, and centuries later it was in the region of Zebulun and Naphtali that a great light dawned — the district where Jesus began His public ministry, exactly as Isaiah had foretold (Matt 4:13-16). The smallest branch of Jacob's family became the neighbourhood where the Messiah preached.

Nobody looking at this list could have guessed that.

Small beginnings run right through Scripture. A mustard seed. Five loaves. Twelve ordinary men. A stable in Bethlehem. God consistently starts with what looks too small to matter.

If your life, your ministry, your church or your family feels small, take heart. God is not counting the way we count. He is not impressed by size, and He is not discouraged by its absence. What matters is not how much you have but whose hands it is in.

Do not despise the day of small things (Zech 4:10).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where do you feel that what you have to offer is too small to matter?
2. How has God used something small in your life?
3. Are you measuring your life by size or by faithfulness?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are not impressed by size and You are not discouraged by smallness. Take what little I have and use it however You choose. Amen.
